findings.title: Same concurrent-delete NPE remains on subgroup stream lookups
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() now treats a null modelSupplier.get() as a missing group, but getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer), and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. modelSupplier is the same LazyModel around getGroupById that returns null when the cached group was deleted by another request. Those three methods are used by subgroup listing and search, so the same race still throws NullPointerException and fails the admin call instead of degrading. They need the same null handling (and should not assume the delegate is present).

findings.title: Missing group makes getSubGroupsCount return null
findings.body: When the persistence delegate has disappeared, getSubGroupsCount() returns null rather than a count. GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount writes that value straight into GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount, so a brief group list that races with deletion now succeeds but emits a null subGroupCount for a group that is still in the response. Callers that unbox GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() (comparisons or arithmetic) still NPE; a deleted group has no children, so this path should return 0L.

findings.title: Concurrent group test can pass without observing the race
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader, deletes the groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader or checking that it ran. The reader can still be inside groups() when the assertion runs, so an NPE from that in-flight call is recorded only after the test has already passed; conversely the deletes can finish before the thread is scheduled, so the test passes without ever overlapping read and delete. The thread is also left running with the shared admin client into later tests. Join it (with a timeout) before the assertion, and fail if it never completed a read.
